checkpoints.question: Which of the following is a required section within a complete Incident Response Plan?

options.A: A list of all approved security vendors and their contract terms
options.B: A schedule of all employees' work hours and on-call rotation dates
options.C: A detailed inventory of every asset on the network with its physical location
options.D: A statement of management commitment and authority granted to the response team

checkpoints.explanation: The IRP must include a policy statement that covers management commitment and the authority granted to the response team. The other options are not listed as required IRP sections.

checkpoints.question: A dedicated CSIRT structure is characterized by which of the following traits?

options.A: External consultants hired on a per-incident basis with flexible pricing
options.B: Full-time IR professionals with the fastest response time but higher cost
options.C: A small dedicated core plus on-call specialists coordinated with external vendors
options.D: Employees from multiple departments with IR as a secondary role and lower cost

checkpoints.explanation: The dedicated CSIRT model uses full-time IR professionals, providing the fastest and most practiced response but at higher expense. Virtual and hybrid models are cost-effective alternatives with different trade-offs.

checkpoints.question: Why should a retainer agreement with an external IR firm be signed before an incident occurs?

options.A: To establish contractual SLA terms and response obligations before crisis negotiation becomes difficult
options.B: To restrict the firm from providing services to your organization's direct competitors
options.C: To create a backup communication channel if the primary incident response team is unavailable
options.D: To guarantee IR services at no cost regardless of incident severity or scope

checkpoints.explanation: A pre-signed retainer agreement defines response-time SLAs and commercial terms in advance, so negotiation does not delay response during an active incident. The other options misstate the purpose of retainer agreements.

checkpoints.question: Which document type contains exact commands and tools for specific tasks like memory capture or disk imaging?

options.A: An IRP policy documenting management authority levels and organizational commitment to response
options.B: A playbook defining decision trees for incident escalation and regulatory notification steps
options.C: A runbook containing exact tactical commands and tools for memory capture and disk imaging
options.D: A CSIRT charter outlining team roles, responsibilities, and on-call rotation requirements

checkpoints.explanation: Runbooks contain exact tactical and technical procedures, including specific commands and tools, so responders follow the same steps without needing to recall details under stress. Playbooks guide strategic decisions, not technical execution.

checkpoints.question: Under GDPR, what is the notification deadline for a data breach discovery?

options.A: 72 hours to the supervisory authority after discovery
options.B: 60 days to the supervisory authority and affected individuals
options.C: 24 hours to law enforcement and affected individuals
options.D: 30 days to the organization's insurance provider and legal counsel

checkpoints.explanation: GDPR requires notification to the supervisory authority within 72 hours of discovery. The other timeframes do not match GDPR requirements.

checkpoints.question: Why is need-to-know restriction important when communicating during an active incident?

options.A: To satisfy data privacy regulations governing who may access breach information
options.B: To ensure senior leadership has primary visibility into breach scope and details
options.C: To prevent alerting insiders or active attackers to limit pivot attempts or escalation
options.D: To reduce meeting frequency and accelerate incident decision-making speed overall

checkpoints.explanation: Need-to-know restriction keeps information compartmentalized to avoid alerting an insider threat or an active attacker to take evasive action before they are fully ejected from the environment.

checkpoints.question: What is the primary purpose of a tabletop exercise in incident response training?

options.A: To test the organization's capability to restore all critical systems after failure
options.B: To conduct discussion-based scenario walkthroughs with mid-scenario injects for complexity
options.C: To verify a specific component like backup restoration or notification timing
options.D: To run IR procedures against test systems in a controlled live environment

checkpoints.explanation: A tabletop exercise is discussion-based and may include scenario injects to force adaptive response, but does not activate real systems. Full-scale exercises test actual procedures; functional exercises test single components.

checkpoints.question: Which NIST publication is the authoritative incident planning framework reference for the Security+ exam?

options.A: NIST SP 800-34 provides Contingency Planning and business continuity guidance
options.B: NIST SP 800-88 contains Guidelines for Media Sanitization and data destruction
options.C: NIST SP 800-53 covers Security and Privacy Controls and compliance requirements
options.D: NIST SP 800-61 is the Computer Security Incident Handling Guide framework

checkpoints.explanation: NIST SP 800-61 is the authoritative Computer Security Incident Handling Guide and the primary framework reference for Security+ incident planning content.
